reader.requirement: On an indexed REWRITE, an alternate key whose value is unchanged keeps the record's retrieval position under that key; a changed key may reorder it, and when duplicates are allowed the record goes last in the duplicate set of its new value; this holds for every access mode and record form 1985 allows.

edition-consulted.switches: COBOL-85-only mandatory INVALID KEY phrase on REWRITE/START (Year < 2002); syntax only, not this rule's behaviour
refuses the 2002 RECORD word / FILE phrase forms at 85

reader.edition-search: grep 'Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior' over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO/*.cs: the only indexed-connector edition reads are IndexedConnector#SelectSequentialRecord (IndexedReadPreviousAfterOpenAtEnd, READ PREVIOUS only) and #ReadRandom (IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly, random READ '02' only); neither is on this rule's path. KeyedIoEmitter has no edition read. Rewrite re-stamps a fresh release ordinal only for keys whose value (collating order) changed.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the runtime REWRITE path is edition-blind; 85 refuses only the later phrases (SUPPRESS WHEN, SOURCE, RECORD word)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers dynamic access with an unchanged key and a key changed away and back; not sequential access, a varying-length record, a unique alternate key, figurative values, or the failure path

probes.printed: A-UNCH: AA 01 02 03; B-TOCC: CC 04 02; B-BACK: AA 01 03 02; unique key changed U3->U0 walks 03 01 02 04; dup unique -> 22; order survives CLOSE (identical at --std 2023)
probes.expected: GR15a unchanged order; GR15b last in the duplicate set; GR16c 22

probes.printed: sequential access RECORD VARYING 4..12: S1=00 NEXT=02; S3=02; BB set 01(LN 4) then 03; AA 02 LN=12
probes.expected: the changed record goes last in BB; lengths kept

probes.printed: HIGH-VALUES/LOW-VALUES keys: order 03 01 02; REWRITE after a failed READ -> 43
probes.expected: LOW-VALUE first, then the HIGH-VALUE set in its order of entry

probes.printed: COBOL0900 the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase ... requires COBOL-2023 (targeting COBOL-85)

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR15  (4.6.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR15

reader.notes: One release ordinal per key in the frame; Rewrite gives a fresh ordinal only to keys whose value changed (GR15a/b), and Duplicates refuses a unique collision with 22. Every probe matched the 1985 text and was the same at --std 2023.

refuter.evidence: Read IndexedConnector#Rewrite: 'changed' is decided per alternate key from AlternateValue over the record area image (so a key described in another 01 is covered), and only changed keys get a fresh ordinal. I read the definitions it depends on: §1985:IX.2.5.4 GR4 (a key written through another record description) and §1985:B.2.2 (indexed files use the native collating sequence even under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE). Probe q5_alt2nd01.cob (--std 85, sequential access) rewrote through a second 01 that does not name the alternate key (B-ALT-N PIC 99 over R-ALT). Unchanged 11 -> 00, and the record keeps first place. 03 changed to 12 and back to 11 -> 02 and goes last: walk 02 11, 04 11, 03 11, 01 AA. Same unique U -> 00; the next REWRITE without a READ -> 43 (GR2). Probe q4_pcs.cob ran with PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS REV (Z..A): walks and START stayed in native order (01 AA, 02 BB, 03 CC), and after a REWRITE into the AA set the walk was 01 AA, 02 AA. cite.py: OK §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR15 the text is in GR15; OK §1985:IX.2.5.4 GR4 the text is in GR4; OK §1985:B.2.2 the text is in the clause.
